strings.d1.s0.name: Stortorget
strings.d1.s0.tips: Medieval square lined with colourful houses. Home to the Nobel Museum and the site of the 1520 bloodbath. Quiet in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Royal Palace Stockholm
strings.d1.s1.tips: A palace of 600 rooms. See the State Apartments and the Treasury, and catch the changing of the guard at 12:15 (on horseback in summer).
strings.d1.s2.name: Under Kastanjen Gamla Stan
strings.d1.s2.tips: Courtyard café under chestnut trees. Try the meatballs and a kanelbulle (cinnamon bun).
strings.d1.s3.name: Mårten Trotzigs Gränd & Prästgatan
strings.d1.s3.tips: The narrowest alley in the city, just 90 cm wide. Look for the runestone, and escape the tourist crowds of Västerlånggatan.
strings.d1.s4.name: Riddarholmen Church & Monteliusvägen
strings.d1.s4.tips: Royal tombs (summer), then a sunset view of Gamla Stan from the cliffs of Södermalm.
strings.d1.b0.name: Nobel Prize Museum
strings.d1.b0.tips: See the Nobel chairs (signed underneath). A good alternative to wandering the streets.
strings.d1.b1.name: Kaffekoppen Stortorget
strings.d1.b1.tips: Café on the square; time for fika.
strings.d2.s0.name: Vasa Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: A 69 m warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 (98% original). One of the world's best museums; opens at 09:00.
strings.d2.s1.name: Skansen
strings.d2.s1.tips: The world's first open-air museum (1891). Swedish village houses, elk, reindeer and wolves, plus dancing in summer.
strings.d2.s2.name: Skansen Solliden Restaurant
strings.d2.s2.tips: A restaurant with views inside Skansen; meatballs.
strings.d2.s3.name: ABBA The Museum
strings.d2.s3.tips: Sing on stage with ABBA. Timed tickets, book online.
strings.d2.s4.name: Rosendals Trädgård
strings.d2.s4.tips: Greenhouse café in winter; try the hot chocolate.
strings.d2.b0.name: Nordic Museum
strings.d2.b0.tips: Scandinavian everyday culture, including the Sami. An alternative to ABBA.
strings.d2.b1.name: Blå Porten Djurgården
strings.d3.s0.name: Fotografiska
strings.d3.s0.tips: Photography museum in a former customs house. The rooftop café overlooks the harbour, and it's open until 23:00.
strings.d3.s1.name: Nytorget & SoFo
strings.d3.s1.tips: Hipster Södermalm with vintage shops, and the neighbourhood of Greta Garbo.
strings.d3.s2.name: Meatballs for the People
strings.d3.s2.tips: 14 kinds of meatballs (including elk and reindeer) in SoFo.
strings.d3.s3.name: Skinnarviksberget
strings.d3.s3.tips: The highest natural point in the city. Views over Riddarfjärden; bring a picnic.
strings.d3.s4.name: Mariaberget & Monteliusvägen Sunset
strings.d3.s4.tips: A walking path along the cliffs, with sunset views of City Hall and Gamla Stan.
strings.d3.b0.name: Pelikan Södermalm
strings.d3.b0.tips: A beer hall from 1904 serving Swedish classics.
strings.d3.b1.name: Spritmuseum Djurgården
strings.d3.b1.tips: Museum of snaps and akvavit. An alternative to Fotografiska.
strings.d4.s0.name: Stockholm City Hall
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Nobel banquet is held in the Blue Hall; the Golden Hall has mosaics. Visit by guided tour only. The tower (summer) is 106 m.
strings.d4.s1.name: Drottningholm Palace
strings.d4.s1.tips: UNESCO-listed home of the royal family, with a baroque garden and the Chinese Pavilion. Take the boat from Stadshuskajen (1 hour, summer) or the metro plus bus.
strings.d4.s2.name: Drottningholm Palace Theatre
strings.d4.s2.tips: A baroque theatre from 1766 with original stage machinery. Visit on a tour.
strings.d4.s3.name: Drottningholms Paviljong Café
strings.d4.s3.tips: Café in the palace gardens; open sandwiches (smörgås) and fika.
strings.d4.s4.name: Lovön Island Walk
strings.d4.s4.tips: Along the shore of Lake Mälaren. Return by boat or bus.
strings.d4.b0.name: Millesgården Lidingö
strings.d4.b0.tips: Terraced garden museum of the sculptor Carl Milles. An alternative to Drottningholm.
strings.d4.b1.name: Stadshuskällaren
strings.d4.b1.tips: The Nobel menu (from past years) in the City Hall cellar.
strings.d5.s0.name: Waxholmsbolaget Strömkajen
strings.d5.s0.tips: Archipelago ferry (30,000 islands). Vaxholm is 1 hour away; the Båtluffarkortet pass costs 995 SEK for 5 days.
strings.d5.s1.name: Vaxholm Fortress
strings.d5.s1.tips: Island fortress and museum, with the town's wooden houses nearby.
strings.d5.s2.name: Vaxholms Hembygdsgård Café
strings.d5.s3.name: Grinda Island
strings.d5.s3.tips: In winter, Vaxholm and Fjäderholmarna (20 minutes) are enough: snow and ice.
strings.d5.b0.name: Fjäderholmarna
strings.d5.b0.tips: The island closest to the city (20 minutes), with craftspeople and a restaurant.
strings.d5.b1.name: Grinda Wärdshus
strings.d6.s0.name: Östermalms Saluhall
strings.d6.s0.tips: Gourmet food hall from 1888. Try the fish at Lisa Elmqvist, and have a fika.
strings.d6.s1.name: Uppsala Cathedral
strings.d6.s1.tips: 40 minutes by train. The largest cathedral in Scandinavia, with the tomb of Gustav Vasa and Linnaeus.
strings.d6.s2.name: Gustavianum & University
strings.d6.s2.tips: Anatomical theatre from 1620 at Uppsala University.
strings.d6.s3.name: Güntherska Hovkonditori Uppsala
strings.d6.s3.tips: Pastry shop from 1870. Try the prinsesstårta (green marzipan cake).
strings.d6.s4.name: Gamla Uppsala
strings.d6.s4.tips: Viking royal burial mounds and a museum. Take bus 2 there and the train back.
strings.d6.b0.name: Sigtuna
strings.d6.b0.tips: Sweden's oldest town (980), with runestones. An alternative to Uppsala.
strings.d6.b1.name: Hambergs Fisk Uppsala
strings.d7.s0.name: Rålambshovsparken
strings.d7.s0.tips: Waterside park with views of Västerbron bridge.
strings.d7.s1.name: Vete-Katten
strings.d7.s1.tips: Pastry shop from 1928. Try a kanelbulle or a semla (February) for a farewell fika.
strings.d7.s2.name: Drottninggatan & Sergels Torg
strings.d7.s2.tips: Pedestrian shopping street. Visit NK and Kulturhuset, and pick up a Dala horse as a souvenir.
strings.d7.s3.name: Arlanda Express Centralen
strings.d7.s3.tips: The 20-minute express train. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Hallwyl Museum
strings.d7.b0.tips: A palace-home from 1898, free to enter. An alternative to shopping.
strings.d7.b1.name: Café Pascal Norrmalm
strings.note0: The SL card covers 72 hours, including Djurgården tram 7 and the ferry. Arlanda Express costs 340 SEK (Flygbussarna 130). No cash needed: cards are accepted everywhere (Swish).
strings.note1: In winter it's around -5°C and dark by 15:00. In December there's the Christmas market in Gamla Stan and Lucia (13 December), and the Vasa is quiet. Cherry blossom in Kungsträdgården in April and May, semla in February.
strings.note2: Meatballs 200 SEK, fika 80-110, restaurants 300-500, museums 150-280. For a tip, round up the bill. It's an expensive city. Work out whether the Stockholm Pass (Go City) pays off for the museums.
strings.note3: Be at the Vasa for the 09:00 opening. ABBA has timed online tickets. The City Hall tour is mandatory. In summer, take the boat to Drottningholm (1 hour): it's a pleasant trip.
strings.note4: Fika culture: kanelbulle (on 4 October, its own day!), kardemummabulle (cardamom bun), prinsesstårta; also smörgåsbord, gravlax and surströmming (fermented herring; not for the faint-hearted).
strings.note5: Systembolaget (the state liquor store) closes at 20:00 and is shut on Sundays. A beer in a bar costs 80 SEK.
strings.transit.name: SL 72 hours + optional Stockholm Pass
strings.transit.why_chosen: Covers metro, buses, tram 7 and the Djurgården ferry; 72 hours costs about 350 SEK
